final_proof:
Let Log(u) := {w ∈ ℂ : e^w = u} for u ≠ 0, and let Sq(q) := {s ∈ ℂ : s² = q}. We first establish, for every z ∈ ℂ, the precise identity

    {w ∈ ℂ : sinh w = z} = ⋃_{s ∈ Sq(z²+1)} Log(z+s).     (1)

Suppose first that sinh w = z, and set u=e^w. Then u≠0, and

    z = (u-u⁻¹)/2

is equivalent, after multiplication by 2u, to

    u²-2zu-1=0,

or, equivalently, (u-z)²=z²+1. Thus s:=u-z belongs to Sq(z²+1), u=z+s, and w∈Log(z+s). This proves the inclusion from left to right in (1).

Conversely, suppose s²=z²+1 and w∈Log(z+s). Put u=e^w=z+s. Notice that z+s cannot vanish, because

    (z+s)(z-s)=z²-s²=-1.

Furthermore,

    u²-2zu-1=(z+s)²-2z(z+s)-1=s²-z²-1=0.

Since u≠0, division by 2u gives (u-u⁻¹)/2=z. As u=e^w, this says sinh w=z and proves the reverse inclusion. Hence (1) holds.

Now let q≠0 and use the multivalued argument

    arg q := {θ ∈ ℝ : q=|q|e^{iθ}}.

Then

    Sq(q) = {√|q| e^{iθ/2} : θ∈arg q}.                 (2)

Indeed, every number on the right squares to |q|e^{iθ}=q. Conversely, if s²=q and s=|s|e^{iφ}, then |s|=√|q| and 2φ∈arg q, so s has the displayed form. In particular, replacing θ by θ+2π changes the displayed root to its negative, so the multivalued argument supplies both square roots.

For z²+1≠0, substitute q=z²+1 into (2) and then into (1). This gives exactly the logarithmic expression in Definition 2. The additional term 2kπi does not alter the set when ln is already the multivalued logarithm: for every integer k,

    Log(u)+2kπi = Log(u),

because e^{w+2kπi}=e^w, and translation by −2kπi proves the reverse inclusion. If ln were instead taken to mean the principal logarithm, allowing all k∈ℤ would produce Log(u) and lead to the same result.

There is, however, a necessary zero-case correction. Under the standard definition, arg 0 is undefined. When z=±i, one has z²+1=0, so Definition 2 as literally printed is undefined, while Definition 1 is not: for example, sinh(iπ/2)=i and sinh(−iπ/2)=−i. Thus the universal equivalence, read literally with the standard domain of arg, is false at z=±i.

The correction is to stipulate that the radical term √|q|e^{(i/2)arg q} means 0 when q=0, or, equivalently and more cleanly, to formulate it using Sq(q). Since Sq(0)={0}, identity (1) then gives

    sinh⁻¹(i)=Log(i),    sinh⁻¹(−i)=Log(−i).

Consequently, with this necessary zero-case convention, Definitions 1 and 2 define the same multifunction for every z∈ℂ. Without that convention, the second displayed definition is not defined at z=±i and the claim requires precisely the correction just stated.
